theBigPicture: The US-Iran war enters its eighth month with President Trump warning Iran could target American cities, while oil prices remain elevated despite a sharp one-day drop. At home, a record-late first Atlantic hurricane threatens the US Gulf Coast this weekend, and France is gripped by student protests over debt-driven austerity. Markets remain oddly calm, with investors betting the worst of the war premium is priced in for now.

householdImpact.energyAndFuel: Oil prices fell sharply today but remain high because of the war in the Middle East, so expect gas pump prices to stay elevated rather than drop back to normal. Natural gas prices are steady, meaning home heating bills shouldn't spike this month.
householdImpact.borrowingAndMortgages: Financial markets are calm and lending conditions are easy, which helps keep mortgage and auto loan rates from climbing further. Credit card rates remain high, so paying down balances is still the smartest move.
householdImpact.groceriesAndSupplyChain: Persistently high oil prices raise the cost of shipping and trucking food, which slowly works its way into grocery prices. No major supply chain disruptions are hitting shelves right now, but the war premium keeps a floor under prices.
householdImpact.jobsAndSavings: With markets calm and borrowing conditions loose, layoffs aren't being driven by financial stress, which is good news for job security. Retirement accounts are holding steady, though a hurricane landfall or escalation in the Middle East could jolt markets quickly.

globalFlashpoints.summary: Trump says he'll speak 'very soon' with Putin, partly over Russia's plague lab death, keeping diplomatic channels open but the war grind unchanged.

The US-Iran war continues into its eighth month with Trump claiming 'nobody knows who is running Iran,' while Saudi and Houthi forces battle across Yemen and bombers were pulled from a UK base over drone attack fears.
Anger is boiling in Japan and Okinawa after a US Marine was arrested for killing a local woman, straining the American military presence in the region.
Hundreds of thousands of French high-school students are clashing with riot police over austerity, while Venezuela's worsening blackouts are fueling public fury.

topStories.headline: Record-late first hurricane of the season threatens US Gulf Coast by Saturday
topStories.whyItMatters: A tropical depression in the Gulf is forecast to become the season's first hurricane — the latest first hurricane since 1905 — with a possible US landfall this weekend. Coastal residents should review storm prep now, as supply runs on generators and essentials are already starting.

topStories.headline: Trump warns Iran could 'take out' LA and San Diego as war hits month eight
topStories.whyItMatters: The President's stark comments about Iran's reach have alarmed West Coast residents and raised the stakes in an already tense conflict. Any escalation could send oil — and your gas prices — sharply higher.

topStories.headline: France in crisis as student riots meet debt and tax pressure
topStories.whyItMatters: Riot police used tear gas against hundreds of thousands of protesting high-schoolers as France grapples with mounting debt. European political instability can ripple into global markets and energy prices.

topStories.headline: Paramount-Warner Bros merger closes, putting CNN and CBS under one roof
topStories.whyItMatters: The newly combined media giant, trading as Skydance, now controls two major US news networks. Media consolidation shapes what news you see and how it's covered.

topStories.headline: Kenya reports first-ever Ebola death after traveler arrives from DRC
topStories.whyItMatters: Health officials are tracing contacts after a man traveled through Uganda into Kenya. Quick containment matters for regional travel and trade — and it follows a separate plague scare in Russia that the WHO says is under control.

whatWeAreWatching: Whether Tropical Depression Nine strengthens into the Atlantic's first hurricane and where it makes landfall this weekend — watch fuel and generator prices if it hits populated areas.
Trump's promised call with Putin and whether Moscow offers more transparency on the plague lab death.
The battle for Yemen between Saudi-led forces and the Houthis, which could disrupt Red Sea shipping and push oil prices back up.
Whether France's student protests spread into a broader national movement against austerity.
The Cook Political Report's shift toward Democrats in key Senate races, an early signal for next year's midterm battles.
